title: WHICH CULTURAL LENS DO MODELS ADOPT? ON CULTURAL POSITIONING BIAS AND AGENTIC MITIGATION IN LLMS
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures cultural positioning bias. In relation to religion, it specifically measures the tendency of LLMs to use stereotypical religious language and concepts (e.g., 'prophet', 'devotion', 'sacrifice' for Pakistan; 'orthodox' for Russia) when generating content about certain non-US cultures, framing them from an 'outsider' perspective.
findings: LLMs tend to use stereotypical and traditionalist language when generating content for non-US cultures. For instance, salient terms for Pakistan included religious references like 'prophet,' 'devotion,' and 'sacrifice,' and for Russia, 'orthodox' was a salient term. This indicates that models often reduce complex cultures to simplified, often religious, stereotypes, reinforcing an 'outsider' viewpoint.
